utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, please, my name is Niemann, and I appear with my colleagues, Ms. McMurrey, Mr. Turone, and Mr. Huber for the Prosecution, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I am Edina Residovic, Defence Counsel for Mr. Zejnil Delalic, along with my colleague, Eugene O'Sullivan, professor from Canada. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I am Zeljko Olujic, Defence Counsel for Mr. Zdravko Mucic, along with my colleague, Niko Duric, attorney from Croatia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I am Salih Karabdic, attorney from Sarajevo, Defence Counsel for Mr. Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I am Cynthia McMurrey, and along with my colleague, Nancy Boler, we represent Esad Landzo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we have the witness now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I completed the examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Defence for Mr. Mucic does not have any questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence of Mr. Hazim Delic does not have any questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence of Esad Landzo does has no questions for this witness either. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Prosecution, any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, did you have or have you ever had a nickname or street name of Sokol, S-O-K-O-L?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the war, and possibly afterwards, did you know Mr. Delalic having a name or being referred to as Oganj?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: In my knowledge, he used a code name of Ikar in one operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you ever know him by the name of Oganj?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: No. I believe an operation was called Oganj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You never at any stage wrote to him in a private capacity, after the war, and addressed a letter to him as Oganj and signed it Sokol?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now, I think Judge Jan raised a matter yesterday, but I'm not certain that we ever got a clear answer to it. I might ask you the same question again, for the purposes of this record. Were you aware of all the orders, both written and oral, transmitted to or by Mr. Delic during 1992?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: Of course I could not know all of it. I could know only a part.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You said that in May, 1992 the JNA and SDS forces attacked Hadzici. What do you mean by SDS forces?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: Organised and armed units consisting of mainly Serb population, which were then formed into a party of SDS. Prior to that they had training in the JNA barracks, they were already prepared, and learned how to block transportation routes and all the important strategic sites overlooking the town of Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did they operate under any particular name, that you know of?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: No. Those were SDS forces. I know how we would call them, but I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now, did the JNA and SDS forces work together during the attack on Hadzici?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: During the course of the war in 1992, did you or members -- or people under your command ever take prisoners?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where and when did you take these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: In the liberation action of Trnovo and the Operation Strajiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who under your command actually took the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: That was combat soldiers advanced, and then the enemy surrenders, so I cannot name the soldiers who would do that. These would be the units attacking and capturing enemy soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And when the prisoners were taken, where were they kept in prison --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I do not see the relevance of these questions in connection to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I suppose it follows from his own answers, his earlier answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where were the prisoners taken to?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: We would then hand them over to the police units, who would then take care of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know all of the units that were subordinated to TG-1 when Mr. Delalic was the commander?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: I believe I can recall them, but I can't really claim that I will remember them all, but I do know the units. I might omit one or two, but I can list them, if you want me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I would be grateful if you would, and certainly after all this time I wouldn't expect you to remember all of them. So if you can assist us with those that you can remember, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: TG-1 and its commander Zejnil Delalic had a possibility to use the units of the municipal staffs of Jablanica, Konjic, and the municipal staff of the TO of Hadzici. In the meantime, there were units from other municipal staffs who were subordinated to me, and possibly to Mr. Delalic and TG-1. For that reason I cannot recall all of them, because we have units from Vakuf, Zenica, from Rijeka, Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you aware whether all of the members of these particular units were part of the command of TG-1, or were only part of the members of these units part of that command? Now, that may be a confusing question. If it is, please say so, and I'll come back. Did you hear my question?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: I did not understand the question, so I expected that you would continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Niemann, don't you think this detail is better for the witness who is regarded as his chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I don't necessarily need to press it with this witness, Your Honours. I just wanted to explore it with him. But I agree. I'll move on, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know any of the members of the command of TG-1 when Mr. Delalic was the commander; during the time you knew him and were with him, did you know any of the members and, if so, can you tell us who they were?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: I know Mr. Pilica Sucro, who was the head of staff. I know him best of all the others. And then the artillery head, I used to know him, but I can't recall his name right now. Then the communications head also I cannot recall. I'm not very good with names.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. That's fine. I just asked you some questions about -- in the beginning about your nickname, Sokol, and so forth. I just want to show you a document that I would ask the usher to give to you, and just looking at the Bosnian version of that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please have a copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Pass that to Ms. Residovic. She's seen the documents as part of the material discovered to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I don't want to go into details of this personal letter of yours, but I just want you to tell me whether the name of the person arrested and who signed it, but I don't want to go into the details. Just looking at that document, does that appear to be your writing?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: This is my writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And it's signed by you as Sokol, is it?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And am I right in saying it's addressed to Herr Oganj?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: That is also correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And that's a reference to Mr. Delalic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: This was back in 1994. It could be that I have used that -- I don't know for which exact reason. Maybe this was just an association in connection to the action I have mentioned. And you can also see from the letter that it's got social character.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is personal letter, and that's why I don't want to go into the detail of it, but certainly you may read, just to yourself, read through it and see whether you can remember it. My only interest in it is whether you wrote to Mr. Delalic and called him Oganj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Does it really mean much, whether he could assume a particular name?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It means a lot, Your Honour, when we look at the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Because I know so many people who have nicknames to which they have no relation to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it does go to the documents that were discovered in Austria. It does go very much germane to those.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: My question is you were writing to Mr. Delalic in that letter, weren't you? Would you say "yes" or "no", because we need to get it on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And you referred to him here as Herr Oganj?

utterances.speaker: HUSEIN ALIC
utterances.text: I already explained that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Your Honours, I tender that, but not for the contents of it. It's a personal letter, I don't think that it's necessary that the personal details be exposed, but just with reference to the name and the signature on the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (Microphone not on) -- put it to him in cross-examination. Don't you think that is sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I won't press it, Your Honour. I won't press it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted he referred to him as such, even if in a --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If it becomes an issue later on, Your Honours, I can deal with it then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If you are referring to person who has taken part in a particular operation. Just call him by that name, not that only that it is his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Whatever it is, I wouldn't know. There is some uncertainty as to why the name Oganj was used, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Also --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In any case, Your Honours, you have maybe made your decision, but I wanted to express our objection to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I don't press the tendering of it, Your Honours, and I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: (No translation).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This is the end of your testimony. Thank you very much, we are very grateful for your assistance. Can we have your next witness? You are discharged, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning. Could we please call for witness Pilica Sucro.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please swear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Take your seat, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please introduce yourself by stating your full name to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: My name is Pilica Sucro.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pilica, can you tell us where and when you were born?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I was born April 5th, 1953 in the Village of Mirojevici, area of Bistrica, and Bijela Polje (phoen), Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where do you live, Mr. Pilica?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I now reside in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pilica, can you tell us about your formal education?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: After the elementary school, I completed high school, then the military academy in the former JNA. That would be my education for now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is your rank now, Mr. Pilica?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I am a Colonel in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, please tell the Chamber where were you on April 6th, 1992, when the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina began?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: On April 6, 1992, I was in Kiseljak. I was there with the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What rank did you hold in the former JNA, Mr. Pilica?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I was a Major.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, did you at any given moment during 1992, join the defence forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Chamber already has sufficient evidence concerning the legislation of the newly formed state concerning its armed forces formation and establishment. That's why I will not ask you these questions. But could you tell us what were your first military operations in April, 1992, as a member of the TO?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: My first duty, which was of a short period, only several days, was sort of a military counsel to the municipal staff of Kata (phoen). That was only for several days.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pilica, did at any time during 1992 -- form a Tactical Group 1, was it formed, and did you perform any tasks as a member of it?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with its establishment. TG-1 was founded and I was deputy commander of it. I also had the task as the head of staff. Since this was a small command post, there were instances where I was also in charge of operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who appointed you to this post?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I was appointed to this post by the staff of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time, that is, the superior command. And it was the highest command which dealt with military or was in charge of military matters in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pilica, can you recall when you started with your duty as deputy commander or as the chief of staff of the Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, I can recall. This was on 12 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown document P183? Is it D1? May the English version please be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Put the lights on, the light on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, is this the document of your appointment, and did you personally supply this document to the Defence in this case?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document you are referring to, and I personally submitted it to the Defence, at their request.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, since the witness has recognised this document as his own, and it is relevant for these proceedings, I move to admit it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this document, Mr. Pilica, there is no date of issue, however, you told me that you started on your duty on 12 May 1992. Is it correct that that was the date on which you started your duties?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was your first commander, Mr. Pilica?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: My first commander was Mustafa Polutak, currently General in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was your Tactical Group tasked with?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Our Tactical Group was tasked with lifting of the siege of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pilica, can you tell me whether, in the course of carrying out this task, what was the first operation which your Tactical Group conducted, and in which area or direction did it take place?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: One of the first attempts at breaking through the ring around Sarajevo was in the area Koscanj, that is a village near Hadzici, Batalo Brdo, Rakovica, and if you continued in that direction you go to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, can you remember when this took place?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: This took place in the latter half of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were certain units from Konjic also involved in this task at that time?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, not in that attempt.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, can you remember, given the area of your activity, whether, at some subsequent attempt at lifting of the siege of Sarajevo, units from Konjic did take part?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember. This was in the middle of June, 1992, in the area Pazaric, Hadzici, Sarajevo, and in this attempt there was a unit from Konjic, that is from the territory of the Municipality of Konjic, which took part in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pilica, a moment ago we saw the order of your appointment. In the same order Mr. Mustafa Gagula was appointed. Can you tell me who was in charge of appointing commanders of Tactical Groups?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: It was only the superior command in this period. It was the main staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the commander of Tactical Group or could the commander of Tactical Group appoint members of the Tactical Group staff?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: He could not appoint anyone to duties or to posts, any members of the Tactical Group, but he could nominate and also select people with whom he wanted to work. His nominations would be sent to the superior command through different means of communication, and following that -- for the most part the orders would reflect those nominations and the commanding staff of the Tactical Group 1 would be appointed in such way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, can you tell me how long you were in this -- on this duty of the deputy commander of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I was on this duty until 10 October 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago you said that your Tactical Group was tasked with an attempt to lift the siege of Sarajevo. Throughout the period of time while you were chief of staff of the Tactical Group 1, was this the only task of your Tactical Group? Did it remain the only one?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, it did. From the beginning to end, it was a task -- it was the main task of the Tactical Group, of this group, and of course during this period of time, while I was on this duty, as I stated, it was the case, and even thereafter until the Tactical Group was dissolved.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, did the command of your Tactical Group have a large command or was it a very developed command with many different bodies?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: The principles of organisation of a Tactical Group are such that it is a temporary formation. It was established for specific tasks and, of course, it had a number of officers needed to carry out these tasks. Our Tactical Group had a small staff, and this number varied, basically, between five to eight members throughout the time -- the period within which the Tactical Group existed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, we are not soldiers, but so far we have learned that certain units were subordinate to you in order for you to be able to carry out your task. As a chief of staff of Tactical Group 1 in this period, can you tell me how it was that you carried out your tasks in practice, or how were certain units placed under the Tactical Group command in practice?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Our first task within these activities was to visit all the units under the command of the municipal staffs in order to gather as comprehensive information as possible about the size of troops, the training.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please just hold on a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please go on, sir. You started explaining how you went about putting together the troops that you needed for -- in order to carry out your tasks.

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: When we received complete information on the available troops and resources, we would plan our combat operations within the framework of our task, and we proposed to the superior command the way in which they should be engaged and used.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, did the superior command, and as I understood you, this was the supreme command of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did the superior command then issue orders to you which units were supposed to become subordinate to your command, that is of the Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, of course. After they received our proposals and elaborated plans, the superior command would issue an order, or a decision; which units will, from the municipal staffs of defence would be engaged in the proposed combat operations. Of course, these orders would then reach our command and these were orders which pointed -- indicated what our further involvement and use of these forces would be.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, after this order by the supreme command, did the municipal staff, which was supposed to set aside units, issue their own orders specifying which units are to be subordinate to you?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The municipal staff would order its own units to place themselves under our command for a certain period, and for certain combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, the other units who were -- which were not included in these orders of the staff, under whose command did they remain?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: They remained in the zones of responsibility of the municipal defence staffs, and they were engaged and deployed according to their own plans.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, can you tell me, where was the seat of your Tactical Group, that is Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: In our military parlance we call it a command post, so the command post of the Tactical Group 1 was from the beginning to the end of its existence in Pazaric, in the Pazaric barracks, to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, can you tell me, did there come a time in 1992 when Zejnil Delalic became commander of the Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, there did come a time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you can recall, can you tell me when Mr. Delalic assumed his command duty in Pazaric, that is, when did you turn over your duties to him, that is, when did you show him everything that he needed to know in Pazaric?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I recall that time, I recall those days. It was around 27 July 1992 that we heard that Zejnil Delalic was to take over the command of the Tactical Group 1, and he actually took over on 30 July 1992, and this happened in such a manner that he came to the command post where we did everything that was necessary in order to take over the command. And from there on throughout the period of my staying -- which was 10 October 1992, he remained on duty as commander of Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, do you recall where Mr. Polutak went, based on this order of, as you recall, 27 July 1992?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Of course I do remember. We are very good friends. He went to a new duty, which was larger, a bigger duty. He moved to the superior command, to a part of it, which at that time was located in Visoko. And we called it the Forward Command Post of the main staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, you probably also know who was the commander of this Forward Command Post and, if you do, can you please give us that name?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: This was our current commander, General Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, are you absolutely sure that Mr. Delalic was only appointed on the 27th and took over command on 30 July?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I was only sure when I saw the order of his appointment to commander of the Tactical Group, and this was on the 8th August 1992, that is, several days later. Even though we knew and we believed that he was officially appointed commander of the Tactical Group 1, even when we first heard that he was appointed to this duty, and I mentioned a date, that the date was 27 July.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Until 27 July, are you absolutely certain that the duty of the commander of Tactical Group 1 was carried out by Mr. Mustafa Polutak?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Not only until the 27th, but until the 30th of July. Polutak was officially commander of the Tactical Group 1, that is until the date when I -- as I stated, the command was transferred. And this was at a command post in Pazaric.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a hypothetical question, Colonel. If someone was to tell you or show you a document, according to which Mr. Zejnil Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1 on 18 July, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I do not know. I did not see such a document, such appointment. Personally, I did not see such document. The first appointment which was in written form, I told you when I saw it. I told you the date. And it did arrive at the command post of the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you are completely certain that Commander Polutak was carrying out his duty until the date that you mentioned, 27th, that is the 30th of July?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, I am absolutely certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After Mr. Delalic took over the duties of commander of Tactical Group 1 on 30 July, did you, Mr. Pilica, at that time inform him of an order that a gun from Konjic was to be transferred to the zone of your operation?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Of course I did inform him of that, and this gun is an event that is a good reminder of the events of that period, because my speciality is artillery and even a single gun in that period meant a lot for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, do you remember whether, with respect to the transfer of this artillery piece, there were certain problems with the municipal staff in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, there were. There were -- the problem was a sizeable one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the municipal staff try to verify whether this order actually came from the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Of course they did verify, because they are under the command of the supreme command, and not under our command. So that's one issue. And the other issue was that they badly needed this artillery piece to carry out their own combat tasks in their zone. However, when they saw that this was an order from the commander Sefer Halilovic, they did not continue having a problem with it, and this artillery piece was transferred to its new destination, which was set by the supreme command, and I personally was involved in organising the transfer of this piece to its new emplacement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, when Mr. Delalic took over the duty from Mr. Polutak, did he also take over the same combat task given to Mr. Polutak?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes. Exact same task.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, you said that you had a first attempt at lifting the siege in May, then the second in June, and then in this second one some units from Konjic took part. Can you tell me, at that period when these certain units from Konjic were involved and Mr. Polutak was in charge, did Mr. Delalic have any command responsibilities with respect to these units from Konjic which were subordinate to you during this period in 1992?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I know that he did not have any command duties, and that during this period he engaged, among other tasks, of which I am not aware, but I know that he was supplying -- that he had supplied the unit which was sent to us for this combat operation, and he supplied them in terms of clothes, footwear. And I remember that it was the best equipped unit that we had. This had a special impact in combat moral and psychologically. And I think in turn it had an effect that during that period it was the only unit who actually carried out its task. And to us soldiers, this meant that it had been well prepared, both in terms of the equipment and its morale, and in terms of professional military training.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. When Mr. Delalic took over the duty, during that time or some other time whilst you were his chief of staff, do you know that Mr. Delalic was a commander of all the formations within your area of activity?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I heard of it, but I never saw anything in a written form. For us soldiers, there is no such an order stating commander of all the formations, and we did not accept it in the military meaning of it. I never saw such a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, you have heard of it, but did Mr. Delalic, was he ever a commander of all the formations, or did he have exactly the same authorities as Mr. Polutak?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: He was never a commander of all the formations. He had duties and tasks identical to the ones performed by the former commander, Mustafa Polutak.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you have told us that you did not see the document, I will not show it to you, but I will show you another one and ask of you the same question, whether you have ever seen it. Can the witness be shown document D145/6/4, page 896? Colonel, have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown document D146/1? Colonel, during 1992 did you see this document?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, I did. This is a document that came to our command, which gave us the final written proof of Mr. Zejnil Delalic as a commander of TG-1. It is signed by the President of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, as the supreme commander of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see at the top, the date of issue of the order, and you also see the date of filing around sendout, which was August 17th. Since the Chamber, by this time, has a picture of how documents and orders were transmitted, my question to you is: During 1992 were there occasions that one document comes somewhat later, or that a latter document comes before the one that was dated earlier?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, it was possible, because we had very poor communications. It would happen that sometimes a certain document would be transmitted very quickly, either through a messenger or through some other means which we would have to choose, but the largest number of orders would be transmitted through radio communications. For a brief period of time at the beginning of the war we had telephone links, but at the period of Delalic's command there were no telephone lines, because, in the area of the town of Hadzici, railroads were blown up by the enemy, damaging the telephone lines. And we were unable to use it from then on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, you have stated clearly that by the order of the supreme command, a part of units were subordinated to you, also on the basis of that you said that municipal staffs under the order of the main staff subordinated equipment to you. During the time when you were the chief of staff of TG-1, was there an obligation put on municipal staffs, following the order of the supreme command, for those municipal staffs to forward to you intelligence data?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes. Because we as a temporary command did not have means or personnel who would gather intelligence about the enemy. We usually had only one officer who would coordinate this work and take care of the fulfilment of that particular task. Therefore, all the data necessary to ask you to carry out our tasks had to be gathered through municipal staffs, i.e. their bodies and units. To remind the Chamber that these were data about the enemy, from the front line to the back -- to the rear of the enemy. It was very seldom a counterintelligence activity in our area.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, since we have already heard about the preparations for operation JUG and so on, were there some unpleasant surprises, that is the enemy activities within your area during your preparations for the operations, and did such surprises cause you to react and to look to communicate with the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, there were such cases. There were activities of reconnaissance and sabotage units by the enemy in the area of the front-line and deeper into our area. And the example that was most severe was the wounding of Mr. Catic Djuberko, and the killing of Jozo Fadil as well as wounding of other people who were in that mission. Their task was the one of reconnaissance during the preparation phase for the operation JUG. The presidency of our state and the city of Sarajevo expected a lot from that particular operation. That was an operation that was being prepared for a long time, it was of crucial importance, and we expected to lift the siege finally.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now move on from the preparation for the operation. This incident that you mentioned that was very shattering to you. After it, in your personal knowledge, did there come a directive or an order from the supreme command which was aimed at strengthening the obligation of municipal staffs, in view of co-operation -- their co-operation with Tactical Groups in relation to intelligence data and other issues connected to those bodies?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Even earlier we undertook some measures concerning intelligence at all levels. And we were also bound by certain rules and manuals, but after this particular incident reaction was very resolute, and it also came from the level of our supreme command, from their bodies, resulting in additional directives and warnings concerning intelligence providing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness now be shown P244, the evidence for the Prosecution. I apologise, 224. I may have said the wrong number. Colonel, could you quickly read through the document. I do not want you to authenticate it, because you have said before the Chamber that you left TG-1 on October 10th, but in relation to what you have said earlier, I would have a few questions in regard to it. Colonel, does this document have any relation, or does it stem out of a particular directive from the supreme command concerning the obligations of municipal staffs that you have mentioned -- that you personally saw?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, this is a usual military reaction, which was aimed at more serious understanding of the problem, and it stems directly out of directives of the supreme command staff of the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please look at the date. It states November 14th, 1992. Colonel, regardless of the fact that you left for another post, another duty, did you know that during that time there were again intense preparations for another attempt of lifting of the siege of Sarajevo, and the same area between Igman towards -- between Igman and Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with it, because my next duty after TG was chief of staff and deputy commander of a brigade in the Visoko front line, and one of their basic tasks was also to try to lift the siege of Sarajevo from their side, and concerning intelligence data and security, all of us outside the ring had the duty to cooperate and exchange data.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that this next attempt, which was not performed by Tactical Groups, because by that time they were non-existent any more, was it December of 1992, if can you recall?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: From the area of Visoko municipality, there was an attempt. I also know that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We are not concerned with that please confine yourself to the duties of Mr. Delalic as TG-1. Ask him his relations with the Konjic administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, since this is a document signed allegedly by my client, we had to know whether he had the authority and what was the cause of it, and the witness had explained the seriousness of preparations for the third attempt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We've had enough of that (Microphone not on) the task of lifting the siege of Sarajevo. Intelligence was required, so issued directions in accordance with the directive given by the supreme command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: As chief of staff of Delalic. That was why you called him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: So let's have the evidence related to such details --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As the chief of staff, do you know whether Mr. Delalic had the authority to turn to a municipal staff for the carrying out of such tasks?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning paragraph 6, which you can take a look at. Did the commander have the authority to punish municipal chiefs of staff, and what was his authority if his request was not met?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: He had no right to punish chiefs of staff and municipal staffs, but, what he could do, he could submit a report to a superior command in relation to not meeting the duties, not performing the tasks, and not cooperating with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The interpretation was that he could not punish the chief of staff, and the witness said the commander of the staff. The difference is only between the chief and the commander. Did you say that, that he could not punish commanders?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Commanders of municipal defence staffs, because it relates to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, did Mr. Delalic, during his command of TG-1, have authority to appoint or dismiss commanders of municipal staffs or their members?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, he did not. He could propose certain changes to a superior command, but he personally did not have the authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, did your Tactical Group, during the command of Mr. Polutak, and particularly during the command of Mr. Zejnil Delalic, have any authority over institutions such as schools, prisons, hospitals, or any other institutions?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Delalic, at any time while you were there, meaning the 10th of October, or maybe later if you know, receive any particular authorisation to have a duty or an authority over a prison?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the command of Mr. Polutak, and particularly during the command of Mr. Delalic, as a commander of TG-1, did he or other commanders used to transmit orders of the supreme command to municipal staffs or to some other institutions which were in your area of activity, or in some other area which would be outside or remote from the first ring, the first line of the blockade?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, there were such cases during the command of Mr. Polutak, as well as during the command of Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown documents D145, annex 5-D/41 and annex 5-D/42, pages 813 and 818. Could you please take a look at the document dated August 24th, 1992. Can we have the document dated 24th on the ELMO, because now we have the one dated on the 28th. Colonel, we can see that the date here is August 24th, 1992. My first question to you would be: Between the 20th and the end of August, was it a time of intensive daily combat for your Tactical Group, or was it a quiet period in the TG-1 activities?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: This was a period of intensive combat in connection to the operation JUG. And I have just stated that this was an operation that we all expected a lot from.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, during that time did the commander with all of the members of the command of TG-1, were they at the front -- the first front line where the combat was?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, all the members of the command of TG-1 were at the -- at the observation post in Orman, or another part of the command was in the command in Pazarici, which was just behind the hill. We were all very active, situation was complex, and every moment was of grave importance. We even had air strikes, fierce artillery activities, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I go on with this document, could this be a good time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will rise and reassemble at noon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Before we start, I have tried to get in touch with the Victims and Witnesses' Unit. And I hear, Mr. Olujic, you have not been cooperating with them. You have not given them a list of your witnesses. They have not got any idea of who those who you really want to contact and those who you want them to deal with. You perhaps might have tried today to see them. Possibly they might be able to see what they can do and some of your witnesses might not need, perhaps visas and you likely can get them on short notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: With your permission, Your Honours, last night, after you've given us your suggestion, I contacted my collaborators. However, until this morning, I was unable to secure up until now some witnesses for whom I could guarantee that they would appear next week. And this is the reason why I did not contact the Victims and Witnesses' unit, simply because I was not in a position to either give them the exact names, or their locations at which they are at present because some of them are in the third countries. I have given myself a deadline until two o'clock this afternoon, if I do not receive the relevant information, unfortunately, we would not be able to actually provide any witnesses which I have suggested we may be able to provide. There's still a small window of opportunity. I am expecting some telephone calls early this afternoon, but I assure you that we have done everything that we can. Also, I want to assure you that on 22nd, June, when it would be our turn and if the Defence of the first accused do not have any witnesses available, we would be able to provide some witnesses and my colleague, Niko Djuric, did already did make travel arrangements with some of the witnesses for that period of time. We also have to coordinate the appearance of witnesses with the documents that we need to present at the time of their testimony. So we are attempting to comply as best we can. We will know by two o'clock this afternoon and at 2.30, after the afternoon recess, we will tell you whether we could or could not be in a position to comply with our ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't know how you got your date of 22nd of June as the date you expected to, the date the first accused is expected to start another witness. That was not in the projection made by the order of this Trial Chamber. So when the counsel decides on its own in the exercise of its own discretion, perhaps it might be misconceived and will not fall in line with the realities of the situation. What the Trial Chamber is doing is to exhaust all evidence on all remedies for exercising our discretion to manage the proceedings as much as justice of the case demands. I think we've done enough for any reasonable tribunal to assure our intention to carry on with the proceedings according to the rules of this Tribunal. So we have asked you if you could not, then I suppose we come to the conclusion which is inevitable. We indicated what we would do. We do not intend to spend next week without hearing evidence from the witnesses of accused persons. We do not intend. If we are compelled to do so, then we'll take the normal procedure which should apply in such cases. Thank you very much. Will you kindly invite the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please take your seat.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, before the recess I asked you to look at a document of 24 August. You said to my prior questions that there was a practice that commanders did transmit orders to other commands and commanders. Do you know whether you personally in that you know from that period of 1992, do you know anything about this order that Mr. Zejnil Delalic sent to the municipal staff in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, I do know of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you personally witnessed this order which Mr. Delalic received from the supreme command in order to transmit it to the municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, I was present there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, do you know under what circumstances this order arrived? That is, on which duty were you and Mr. Delalic at the time when this order arrived?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: We were involved in the principal task of our Tactical Group as well as our neighbouring groups. We were engaged in the attempt to lift the siege of Sarajevo. That is, we were engaged in the operation JUG. And this was during the most dynamic period of this operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is the English version of this order on the ELMO? It may have been moved during the recess. Is it still there, please?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I believe that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Now I can see it on my monitor too. So as you were saying, this was during the most dynamic period of the Operation JUG, that Mr. Delalic received the order to transmit it to the municipal staff. Can you tell me what Mr. Delalic specifically did at that time?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I do know what he did. Before he went to carry out a task, which was part of the group that was in charge of the Operation JUG, he dictated these points of this document to a typist and he ordered that his messenger, Irfan, that he be dispatched in a vehicle to the municipal staff in Konjic as soon as possible and that this document be handed to the command of the municipal staff in Konjic. And let me just add this. He quickly sketched another couple of things that were on his mind at the time and for which he believed that the municipal staff should know of so that several different issues are handled here, which gives a basis for different courses of action.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, will you please look at the paragraph 5. Is this one of these points and what was the connection? How was that connected with the Tactical Group 1 of which you were a part and of which Mr. Delalic was a commander?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: This was part of the carrying out of the task for the Operation JUG in the area of activity from Bjelinici towards Kalinovik. And the objective was to link up forces in that area and to facilitate the main tasks of the operation JUG. So this was one of this secondary areas with respect to Operation JUG.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We've already heard that the Operation JUG already had these secondary or ancillary areas of operation. Was this area of the Municipality of Konjic one of the of these secondary or ancillary areas with respect to the operation JUG?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. Would you now, please, look at the document of 28 August 1992. And if you will please place the English version of it on the ELMO. Colonel, is this also one of the documents which was transmitted to one of the bodies in the field?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Of course it is, you can see that right away from the preamble of this document, which refers to the order issued by the supreme command staff in Sarajevo and it also gives the reference number. And it also refers to a previous document which we saw just a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you present when this document was drafted or were you not?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I was not present when this document was drafted and I was not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me this date, 28 August 1992, was this also a period of very intensive operations, that is minute by minute combat operations of your group?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can remove the documents. Colonel, can you now tell me whether Tactical Group 1 of which you were a chief of staff had authority to approve or prohibit visits of international organisations to the military facilities?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who had authority to issue such permits?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I know that this was under the authority of the main staff or the supreme command of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, a hypothetical question for you. If you as a chief of staff of a Tactical Group, an international organisation came to you in order to try to organise such a visit, would you be in a position to issue such a permit or would you be in a position to respond in a different way?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Of course we could not have issued such a permit. That is a commander of the Tactical Group could not because it was not in his authority to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But could the commander, or you personally, mediate with the supreme command in order to obtain such a permit?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, we could do that within the limits of the available time and the situation in which we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel do you have any information with respect to the prison in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, I do not have any information, obviously, during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever heard that Zejnil Delalic had any relation to the prison or have you ever heard or seen that he was given some kind of an order regarding authority over any prison and especially Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I have never heard or seen anything of that nature. And this issue was not part of the authority of Tactical Group 1, with exception of the issue of mediation, which we addressed a moment ago, which happened on a couple of occasions. But that was not really done.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you talk about mediation, that was a comment on the document of the 24th?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any other document relating to the prison in the files of your command?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, we did not have any.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, even though you gave a certain number, let me ask you again, did commander of Tactical Group 1 at any point, at any single day during the time when you were chief of staff there to appoint the commander, staff, guards or anyone in the prison in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: He was not authorised to do it and he did not do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, based on your personal knowledge, can you tell the court whether the commander of Tactical Group 1, whether it was Polutak or Delalic, whether either of them ever appointed Zdravko Mucic commander of the prison in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Neither of them did appoint Zdravko Mucic commander of the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were the chief of staff, can you tell the court whether the commander of the prison, of that prison or any other prison in the area in which you were active in Konjic or other places where there may have been active prisons, in other words, did the commander of prison have an obligation to report to Zejnil Delalic as commander of Tactical Group 1 and did you ever see any such document or report at your command in the files?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, he did not have such an obligation and we never received any such report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the international organisation have an obligation to submit any reports of their visits to the prisons and did you in the Tactical Group 1 command ever receive any report by any international organisation?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: We never received any report by an international organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, while you were chief of staff between 12 May and 10 October, was the commander of Tactical Group 1, either Mr. Polutak or Mr. Delalic, authorised to appoint members of the military investigative commission who conducted questioning of prisoners in the prison?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: They were not authorised for that, and they did not do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, can you tell me whether commander of Tactical Group 1 was authorised to discipline military or other persons who may have committed criminal acts or other insubordination acts in the area of the Konjic municipality?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Punishment or disciplining, as we call it, was not part of the authority of the Tactical Group 1, and we did not engage in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, do you know whether Mr. Delalic, or Mr. Polutak, as commanders of Tactical Group 1, had any other authority over the Celebici prison which I have not asked specifically in a separate question? In other words, did they have any other authorities in that regard as part of their duties?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: They had no authority within the framework of their duties with respect to Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the Operation JUG, if you remember, because you were directly involved with combat units and activities, did Tactical Group 1, during the operation, have subordinated units which were coming from Konjic?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Do you mean the municipal defence staff of the Municipality of Konjic or some other units?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember whether, during the Operation JUG in the area of Orman and so forth, where you were active, did you have a subordinate combat unit from the municipal staff of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, do you know whether those units were engaged at all in the Operation JUG and, if so, do you know where they were engaged?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I know they were engaged in the Operation JUG, but within the area of Trnovo, and the Trnovo front line towards Krupac and further on towards Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, did at any time a guard or some other member of staff in Celebici prison, was he subordinated to the Tactical Group 1 at the time when you were the chief of staff of it?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, do you know whether any of your soldiers, who were subordinate to you during an operation, go to Celebici and commit a crime there?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, nobody did, because there was no need for them to go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While Zejnil Delalic was TG-1 commander, did any of your soldiers commit a crime in some other area? Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Within the period of our command over those units, or groups, there was no such case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Cross-examinations, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, we do not have questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we do not have questions either.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: The Defence of Esad Landzo has no questions of this witness either. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Cross-examination by the Prosecution, please

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Yes, the Prosecution does have cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. My name is Teresa McHenry, and on behalf of the Prosecution I am going to ask you some questions. I am going to ask that you listen carefully to my questions and, if you don't understand them, please just ask me to repeat or rephrase. I'll also tell you that a number of questions I am going to ask may just require a "yes" or "no" answer, and you will not have to repeat things you've already said in direct. So if you can fairly answer a question with a "yes" or "no", please do so, just so we can finish more quickly.

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: (Nod).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Don't nod your head. Say "yes" or "no," because it has to be recorded here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We would like to have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, during the time that you were chief of staff and Mr. Delalic was the commander of Tactical Group 1, who were the other members of the staff?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: There were as follows: Gagula Mustafa, Turkovic, Kiba.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: What was the position of Mr. or Ms. Turkovic?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: It's a Ms. Turkovic. She was a typist. Then Kazazic, Amir. He was an administrative officer. Gagula Mustafa was assistant commander for logistics. And for a brief period of time we also had Turcinovic. We called him Zeka. Also for a brief period we had Rekic, Sead, and later, after Turcinovic, we got Selimovic. I cannot recall his first name. I will eventually. This was the group. Later on we also had Mr. Karic Salko, who, prior to that, was a member of the municipal staff of Hadzici. Selimovic Hamid was the name of the person. This was the command of TG-1, at the moment of the hand-over of duties of a commander of TG-1 when Mr. Delalic took over it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And then during the time that Mr. Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1, did all these people remain in the command staff?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, not all of them remained until the end as members of the command.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Instead of telling me which ones left, maybe what you could do is please tell me who was a member of the command staff in addition to the persons you've already mentioned during any time that Mr. Delalic was commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If you have a particular person in mind, ask him that person, who was there at the time. If you want to use that -- it would be more difficult to remember this pertinent information. It's so long a time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, do you not remember who the members of the command staff were during the time that Mr. Delalic functioned as the commander?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I have mentioned those people already. During the Operation JUG, Selimovic was temporarily transferred to TG-2, due to specific tasks. And if I can recall it correctly, for a brief period of time the typist was also temporarily -- for a brief period of time we had Habiba Veladzic, but I'm not certain about her last name. I don't think there were any additional changes to that. I have mentioned already that Zeka left, and instead of him we got Selimovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: You mentioned during your direct testimony a Mr. Irfan. What was his function?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Irfan was a driver to the Commander Delalic, and in addition to that he would also perform messenger tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And what is his last name? If you don't know, that's fine. You can just say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And how about a Mr. Sultanovic or Mr. Rizvanovic, were they members of the command staff who may have been involved in communication issues?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Rizvanovic was one which was given to us for additional help for a brief period of time, but I did not see him as one of the members of our command.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: So there were people there who worked, in effect, for the command, but were not officially members of the command staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: There were individual cases, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, if I understand you correctly, sir, Mr. Delalic was appointed on the 27th of July, he started functioning on the 30th of July, and then you saw his appointment on the 8th of August. Did I understand you correctly in all respects?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: That is correct, and I have said that on the 27th I heard that he was appointed, but I did not see the written document concerning his appointment until the 8th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And, of course, when Mr. Delalic came on the 30th, you, given that it was a wartime situation, you were waging a war, you and the others accepted Mr. Delalic's authority without requiring written proof of his authorisation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I followed the orders of my then commander, Polutak Mustafa. If he says that Zejnil Delalic is appointed to his post, then all I can say is, "Yes, I understand, commander."

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And then could I just ask that the witness be shown D146 again. Sir, is this the document that you saw on the 8th of August, or was it another document?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: This is the document that I saw on August 8th.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And are you sure it was the 8th you saw it, rather than some day following the 8th?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I saw it on the 8th.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And in the copy, the Bosnian copy that's there, it doesn't actually bear the signature of President Izetbegovic. In the copy that you saw, on the 8th of August, did it actually have the President's signature?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, given the communication problems between Sarajevo and the field, was it an extraordinary event that on the same day that the President signed the document, you would receive it in the field?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: If you have followed my previous statements concerning communications, I accentuated that there were various situations. It would happen that documents would arrive immediately or with a short or a longer, somewhat longer delay. Specifically, if you are interested in this document, I received it, or we received it, rather, by fax in Mount Igman in the Hotel Borik. That's why I could see it right away. And through radio communication, having in mind that Mr. Delalic had already taken over the duty of the commander, and also having in mind the story that there is a certain piece of paper appointing a commander of all formations, which was, of course, questionable to us, we insisted then to receive a definite order as soon as possible, because this was a very responsible command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, can you just explain this a little more, sir. You indicated previously that when Mr. Polutak told you he was commander, and you accepted it without requiring anything more, can you then just explain how was it that you heard about this order for all formations and who it was who insisted that there be clarification? Were you yourself involved in insisting that there be clarification?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: That was not me. I would receive all the information from the commander, Polutak, and what I have just said was the case when I was present, and it did not happen upon my initiative.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, from whom did you hear that the previous order had all units?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I was told that by Commander Polutak.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. And did Mr. Polutak indicate that -- well, let me just move on. And when was it that you heard -- was it on the 30th of July that you heard about this from Mr. Polutak?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I apologise. I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir. You indicate that it was from Mr. Polutak that you heard that Mr. Delalic had been appointed head of all formations, and I am asking when was it that you received this information from Mr. Polutak?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: First of all, this was not all formations, but all the armed forces, all the forces, which is not Tactical Group 1. And I have heard that for the first time around the 27th, as I have stated. Those were the days when one could hear talk about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And if you know, did Mr. Polutak see a copy of Mr. Delalic's appointment, or do you know how Mr. Polutak received his information?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: He was appointed on the 8th of August. He saw it personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir. My question was: When, around the 27th of July, you heard from Mr. Polutak that Mr. Delalic had been named head of all armed forces, do you know how Mr. Polutak had received that information? For instance, do you know if Mr. Polutak saw an appointment order dated the 27th of July?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think the transcript reads he saw it personally. That was his answer to the last question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but let me clarify that, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, when you say he saw it personally, are you referring to the 27th of July document or to the 8th of August document?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I am speaking of the document dated August 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And with respect to the document of the 8th of August, how do you know that Mr. Polutak saw that document? Was he still in the Tactical Group 1 headquarters at that time?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: So there was some period of time when both Mr. Delalic and Mr. Polutak were functioning in the Tactical Group 1 headquarters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (No microphone)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I didn't say functioning as commander, but just were present.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Was there, between the time of the 30th of July and the 8th of August, did Mr. Polutak remain in the headquarters of Tactical Group 1, in any function?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: -- is a fairly difficult one. You mean he continuously was still a member of the TG-1? That's the --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Was he present in the headquarters between 30th of July, when Mr. Delalic took over, and the 8th of August?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I have already said that once.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, could you just explain it a little more. Was he present all the time, some of the time, a little bit of the time? Can you please just give me a little -- so I can better understand what it was and how frequently Mr. Polutak was there.

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Mr. Polutak, to repeat, handed over the duty on July 30th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Thereafter, what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Thereafter, what was he doing there? He handed over the charge on the 30th of July to Mr. Delalic. Thereafter he stayed longer, a little longer, at the same station. What was he doing during that period? This is what the lady wants to ask you.

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, it is clear to me. After handing over the charge, commanders go to their separate duties. I apologise if I was unclear.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And what were Mr. Polutak's duties, after the 30th of July, such that he remained -- such that he was present in the headquarters of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe the witness is being forced to give answers he does not -- would not be true --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (Microphone not on) I think some understanding of the situation --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- and there is an intentional confusion created.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He was still present to discuss appointments of Delalic of the 8th of August. How come that situation? That's all she wants to know. He had already moved to his new formation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I understand the question, but it seems you do not understand me. I apologise. That was war a situation. Commander Delalic was ordered to take over the command in TG-1. Polutak is ordered to move to another duty, and we -- and the front, that is combat, cannot wait for the arrival of a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, let me --

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: The paper arrives when possible, and through other types of communication one can resolve such issues. And this is what we were doing, the issues that present a problem to you, seems to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think, Ms. McHenry, we have to break and reassemble at 2.30. --- Luncheon Recess taken at 1:00 p.m. 1

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Permission to address Your Honours. The problems and difficulties which have appeared with calling of witnesses, my colleague is now going to submit a document with respect to the solution of the problem that we're all seeking. We are still doubtful whether we can accomplish the task. That is, be able to call any witnesses, but we are working in good faith and Your Honours can shortly expect a submission to be handed to you through the registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Your attempt, this afternoon, your first efforts at dealing with the victims and witnesses' unit at giving any of your witnesses. Did you understand my observation? Whether your attempt today is your first effort ever in getting in touch with the victims and witnesses unit? Have you spoke to your witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, with the victims and witnesses unit.
