However, we have been very active in the field, trying to coordinate witness' schedules because we believe that it would be in vain if we would try to put together lists of witnesses for whom we do not realistically expect to be able to respond and be called in this particular time frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He is in the last stage of his witnesses. As the last stage, the last week of his witnesses and after that accused, then you come next. You knew that. And Council for the second accused knew that you're the next person to take over in presenting your case. And you've made no efforts until now. It's not for the Trial Chamber to determine for you to how to organise your Defence. That is essentially the problem of the Council. Anybody expected that right now you should have organised your Defence. Because assistant with the progress of the Defence of the first accused and to say that you are just trying to present particulars for your witnesses, it looks a little awkward.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, with your permission, let me also point out that this is a case of multiple accused. Our own Defence is also based on the witnesses who are being called by the first accused. They may affect our Defence. We, therefore, do not know exactly how many witnesses we need to call. The Defence of the first accused has not been completed and our strategy is being adjusted accordingly. And this is a problem that arises with any case in which there are multiple accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will not repeat why we had the first status conference before the Defence was to open its case. To enable you to go about your defences and streamline them. That's why we held the status conference. We explained in the interest of the accused persons how you should go about it. Instead, various subterranean and open criticisms have come out of our attempt to make life easier for everyone. In any event, I think we'll carry on in the way we've chosen. After the case of the first accused, which must close next week, you have to take over. Let's have the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can take your seat, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mrs. McHenry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Sir, just before the lunch break, we were talking about your information about various appointment orders given to Mr. Delalic. Let me just try to clarify matters and try to ask some questions that I hope will clarify the matter. Did I understand correctly that between the 30th of July and the 8th of August, Mr. Polutak was still present in the headquarters of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: At a command post?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: No, in any function whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: He was not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: So, after the 30th of July, Mr. Polutak was no longer physically present at the Tactical Group 1 headquarters, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, does that mean it's incorrect or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Maybe he was winding up until he stayed on. Because you're confusing as functions or command. Maybe he was not performing any function, maybe he was not in command. But possibly he was present, physically present, to wind up his affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me just ask that sir. After the 30th of July, did Mr. Polutak, was he physically present in any capacity whatsoever in the headquarters of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You're again talking in a capacity, maybe it was privately, to wind up affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, that would include in a private capacity.

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: He was not physically present at a command post of the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We're not talking now about command post. Was he physically present in some other connection in the area where your command post is located? Not at the command post. Maybe he was there in connection with private affairs. She wants to find out, was he physically present in the area on the day of the 30th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well then I may have to go back over a few questions, sir, because I believe there's been some sort of --

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: -- miscommunication or you've remembered things differently, I don't know. But my question is, you indicated that after the 30th of July you learned certain information from Mr. Polutak about Mr. Delalic's authority, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: After 30th of July, I don't know what information you are referring to. Can you please ask me a specific question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, let me go back. You indicated that there was some sort of issue or controversy, or whatever you want to call it, about the scope of Mr. Delalic's authority after the 30th of July, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Objection. The witness said 27th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Come out clearly with what you want. If I guess rightly, you want to clear the discrepancy between Delalic being commander of all forces and the correction of that order. This is what you want to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I would like to hear what this witness' explanation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, do it properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, sir, how was it that you heard about Mr. Delalic having been given authority over all units? Who told you about that and when?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Around 27 July, and commander Polutak.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And you indicated, if I understood you correctly, that after that date there was some discussion and it was decided that the supreme command would be contacted about the issue. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I did not want that, nor do I have such authority, in other words the contact of the supreme command.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did any one, to your knowledge, contact the supreme command about the issue?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I have no such knowledge. But commander Polutak did receive an order from the superior command to turn over the command to the new commander, Delalic. Regardless of the misunderstanding which were existing at the time and which relate to this phrase, "Commander of All Forces." We as command were not entirely clear and so we asked that it be spelled out very precisely in a written form and not to specify all forces, but rather to state directly that this would be Tactical Group 1 because that was its proper name. And I wish this were clear enough now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, sir, I do have a few more questions about it for you. Now, sir, do you know --

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: -- Mr. Polutak saw the order of the 27th of July with the reference to all formations or all armed units?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Objection. The witness has already answered this question before the recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What was his answer then? What was his answer before the recess?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The transcript you can tell that he said that he did not know whether Polutak saw it or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this, sir. If Mr. Polutak informed you that Mr. Delalic had been given authority over all armed units, do you know how Mr. Polutak knew that Mr. Delalic had been given such authority?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: But you're sure that Mr. Polutak was aware of it because he told you about it, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Why do you want him to repeat what he has just said? So you want him to say it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Given the problems, I was going to repeat a few things, but then let me just go forward.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, you indicated that we decided that we wanted some clarification of the authority given to Mr. Delalic and I am asking you who the "we" was?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Command of the tactical group.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you mean Mr. Polutak and yourself or do you mean all members of the staff? Can you just be a little more specific?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Not all members of the staff, but only the inner circle of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And who was part of the inner circle?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: It was the deputy, that is the chief of staff, which was myself and assistance for logistics and for intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And who was the assistant for intelligence?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: It was Zeka, I mentioned him earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: May I ask a question here?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Certainly, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You're a chief of staff of TG-1 at the relevant time. After you received the order of 27th of July, what steps did you take to take to charge over all the formations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not -- that is, I did not receive such an order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He being the chief of staff, would have immediately taken steps to take charge of all the formations, that's what I want. Because he was the next man.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, sir, after you were informed by Mr. Polutak that Mr. Delalic had been given authority over all armed forces, what steps were taken?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Polutak and Delalic conducted a transfer of command of Tactical Group 1 based on the order of the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Next question. Did you, in fact, take charge of all the formations in the areas mentioned in the order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, okay. Sir, going back to the inner circle, you indicated that the inner circle decided to ask for clarification. I would assume that you would agree with me that of the three members of the inner circle, you were the most senior. And my question is, did you, therefore, take any steps to obtain written clarification of Mr. Delalic's authority?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He's already said, it was not within his authority to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, that's why I have asked if he took any steps, even if he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, sir, what was done to obtain clarification?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: First, the other members of the command, and I exclude the commander now, do not have the right of decision taking. So we can only analyse, register and propose. Commander takes decisions on it, the basis of this. So it was only commander Polutak, that is the previous commander was in position to take this decisions or the new commander, that is Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, do you know, was any request or any step whatsoever taken to receive clarification of what of Mr. Delalic's 27th of July appoint?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: So you would agree with me that you don't know that the 8th of August order was in response to any request for clarification of Mr. Delalic's authority? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: It was clear to us when we saw that order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The question is different. Do you know that Mr. Delalic contacted the high command for the clarification of this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And how do you know that, sir?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: From conversation. He asked that through our communications lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And, tell me, were present and you could hear him, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I was not present at the time when he was in communication.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: But Mr. Delalic told you himself that he had requested clarification of his own authority, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: That is not clarification that was not questionable. The authority was clear. It was just the designation of the command, was it TG-1 or what we talked about, commander of all forces? Because commander of all forces meant nothing to us as a Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, then, sir, did Mr. Delalic tell you himself that he requested a further designation of command?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Not to designate it, the command has already been designated.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, sir, what you indicated that Mr. Delalic -- well, you indicated that you learned that the 8th of August order was made in response to some question about Mr. Delalic's command or authority, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: The only issue there was the name, whether a commander, whether it would be the commander of TG-1 or commander of all forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Don't you think you need another question, because I don't see the need to press this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, let me just put it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, you would agree with me that you have no information that the 8th of August --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I have asked you to move to some other question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I will move on, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, the 8th of August order refers to, in addition to Mr. Delalic, it refers to a Mr. Maric. Maybe, in fact, I can ask that the document be shown to the witness. Sir, are you aware of whether or not there was any issue or question about the appointment of Mr. Maric? May I ask that the witness be shown D146, which is the 8th of August document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You are supposed to ask him, does he know Mr. Maric?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, even if he didn't know Mr. Maric personally, he might --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, do you know anything about why in the same order there is also an appointment of a Mr. Maric?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Did Mr. Delalic, to your knowledge, see the 8th of August document?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that frequently, after military appointments had been made, President Izetbegovic confirmed the appointments and then such appointments were published in the Official Gazette? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I don't know what the practice was during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me -- with respect to that document, it refers, and you can look at it if you wish, it refers to a -- that the order is being made pursuant to a proposal from the Minister of Defence dated the 19th of July. Do you know what proposal from the Minister of Defence dated the 19th of July is referred to?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I do not know of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, again, looking at that same document, sir. There is a reference or the designation is for the Tactical Group in the areas Hadzici, Pazaric, Konjic and Jablanica. Now, I certainly understand your testimony, that the Tactical Group was not superior to these municipal areas, but if you can, what does this reference to the municipalities refer to? Does it refer to the zone of operations, does it refer to the municipalities from which units came from? What does this reference here refer to in these four municipalities?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I understood that as a geographical definition of an area or a direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Was it the direction -- was it the area of operations of the Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: That was the general direction, if we take a look at the entire period of activity of TG-1.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: But you would agree it's, according to your testimony, it would not be an accurate description of the area of operation in August of 1992, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Could you please clarify to me in what way is it illogical for it to be an area of operation?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I am not asking you if it's illogical, sir. I am just asking whether or not, in August of 1992, at the time this order was made, is this a correct and accurate description of the municipalities that were the zone of operation of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Specified here is only the line of communication between Jablanica, Pazaric, Konjic, Hadzici, and the areas within it are a wider region that gravitates to that communication.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: So was Konjic one of the main lines of communication for Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Communication, the main communication to which this Tactical Group was tied to, went through Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And when you say "line of communication," what are you referring to? Can you just explain what that means, "line of communication"?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: When I say communication line, I mean the one used for transport, that is roads and rails.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, may I ask now that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 230. And I am finished with D146. Thank you. I'm sorry, can I -- thank you. Sir, did you see this document in August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And does the original Bosnian version, does it bear Mr. Delalic's signature? Do you recognise whether or not that's Mr. Delalic's signature?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Delalic have authorisation to make the appointment reflected in this document?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: He did have the authorities only, and in light of finding temporary solutions to a specific problem until the final appointment arrived, and if it has to do with the emergency engagement of a certain person or to conduct important tasks. And in this particular case this is about a typist, an administrative assistant, who, at the given moment, had to take over a job of the typist who was at that place before, and I have mentioned Ms. Kiba. And if I may add, this needed to be done for the document to become fully valid. So he had the authority only in situations of temporary solutions, if such a person was necessary for a conduct of combat tasks and a superior command was unable for any reasons to go through with that appointment. If I may, even today we have such cases in which the first -- the superior commander writes out a temporary appointment, in the sense of appointing somebody to a function, until the arrival of the final appointment authorised by the superior command. This happens even now during peacetime, and especially during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Surely, the commander can appoint a typist without referring it to the high command.

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: It would be logical, but our superior command appointed all the people, and that was a principle, having in mind the nature of the Tactical Group as a temporary formation, and it deals with tasks limited within a period of time with specifically described duties and tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, do you know why a copy of that document was sent to both the war presidency and the headquarters of Konjic, of the TO Konjic?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I am not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. And let me refer you to the heading there, where it says, "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Armed Forces Supreme Command Staff Sarajevo, Tactical Group 1." Was that the heading for all documents emanating from Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: In principle, this was done in a way that they first mentioned a superior command and then the subordinate command, and this has been put in a correct way, having in mind the rule on official correspondence which we inherited from the former JNA. But I would not rule out the possibility of war documents which did not have such a precisely defined heading of the document. It all depended on people who do that, and we did not have enough trained people who could put through any document in a sufficiently precise manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Turning to another matter, sir. Who took over as deputy commander when you left in October?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: So you did not turn your duties over to any particular person; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I gave my duties over to the Commander Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you earlier spoke about some problems with a gun and the municipal authorities in Konjic. If I understood you correctly, these problems started before Mr. Delalic began functioning as commander of Tactical Group 1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And the supreme command was aware of these problems, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, they were aware.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, during the time that Mr. Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1, in the time that you were there, so from when he began functioning until you left, approximately how many soldiers were subordinated to Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: There were several instances of subordination because there were several attempts at lifting of the Sarajevo siege in accordance with the task of the TG-1, but the number of soldiers never went over 1,200 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: During the time that Mr. Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1, from what municipalities did the units come from, as best you can remember?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I will try to remember. They came from municipalities of Jablanica, Konjic, Hadzici, Kiseljak, Ilidza, and there was one occasion where we had a unit from Prozor, if I recall it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And the units from Konjic, what kind of units were they; in other words, from what entity, TO, MUP?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Those were all units that belonged to the TO, and once we engaged a smaller unit of HOS, exactly at the period of the Operation JUG, and they were engaged in the ancillary area, in the area of Brdo Ormanj towards Brdo Ostrig, and this is the left side of the town of Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Can you just tell -- who are the HOS units? When they weren't subordinated to Tactical Group 1, who were they subordinated to, if they were not part of the TO?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: We then used the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that was a wish of us Bosniaks, to develop such an armed force. It evolved in a completely different direction, but for a period of time also the HVO units, as well as TO units and HOS units, were within those armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: But my question is, if the HOS units were not part of the TO, to whom were they subordinated, when they weren't subordinated to Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: To be honest, I do not know much about HOS units, but they were supposed to be subordinate to the supreme command of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but, from my knowledge, unfortunately, it never came completely true. That was just an effort.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, during the time that Mr. Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1, were any MUP units ever subordinated to him?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And when I say subordinated to him, I mean subordinated to Tactical Group 1. During the time that Mr. Delalic was there, there were never any MUP units --

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, it is clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, during the time that Mr. Delalic was commander of Tactical Group 1, did Tactical Group 1 have any military police, either its own military police or military police units that had been subordinated to it?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, it did not have.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: At any time during the existence of Tactical Group 1, were prisoners captured?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I'm sure these are all questions which have been asked and answered in direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You asked this question --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You asked Mr. Polutak about it, and he answered in the negative.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We are dealing here with prisoners who were detained or arrested when Mr. Polutak was TG-1 commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: During the time that Mr. Delalic was functioning as Tactical Group 1 commander, were any prisoners ever captured during Tactical Group 1 operations?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, there were never.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, you stated in direct that Tactical Group 1 had no authority to discipline the soldiers that were under its command. You would agree with me that there's no regulation or written order which states that Tactical Group do not have authority to discipline soldiers under their command?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: The general principles of organising an engagement of Tactical Groups, it is clearly stated that authorities of the command of a Tactical Group are not to discipline anybody, but they have the right, in relation to individuals or groups who are engaged in misconduct or do not fulfil the tasks, to return them to their parent units and to propose to their command to discipline them. That was the only thing that a TG command could do concerning this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that within the regulations of the Bosnian Army, and within the orders made by the supreme command of the Bosnian Army, that was never stated in writing?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: It is stated in rules that we abided by. These are rules in textbooks inherited from the former JNA, because at that time we did not have any other, and there it is clearly defined concerning the authorities of a Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Were there ever exceptional circumstances, such as, if immediate action was required, or if no other entity was available, to punish a soldier?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: No, there were not such circumstances, and we did not have the right to do it, regardless of circumstances. But their commanders would always monitor, especially if we talk about important combat activities, they would always monitor the conduct of their units and gave help, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, I am going to ask that the witness be shown D145/A/5/D-41, which is 815 and 816 shown to him during direct. Now, sir, this is the 24th of August document, and you indicated that you were present at the time that Mr. Delalic communicated with the supreme command. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I was present when he was drafting the document, and I knew what it was about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do I understand, then, that during the actual communication between Mr. Delalic and the supreme command, you were not present and don't have personal knowledge of what was said?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I was present during the communication. This was done through radio communication, which was only a communication link at that moment. I remember that he reacted because he had more important things to do at that moment, and then I said, "Well, Commander, sir, we should aid, regardless of the circumstances."

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Who was it in the supreme -- who was it in the supreme command that Mr. Delalic was communicating with?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I don't know. I never asked him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: So do I understand, you were not present in the beginning part of the conversation when the persons would have identified themselves; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I was present at that location where it was being drafted, but at that time I was not paying attention who it was concerned. Maybe I knew who the person was, but I did not inquire.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, let me -- you indicated that Mr. Delalic was asked to transmit certain orders and that Mr. Delalic also sketched some other things that were on his mind. Do you remember that, when he was dictating this order?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And what, to the extent that you yourself heard it, what parts did the supreme command ask him to transmit orders about? In other words, I am asking you, what were the things that Mr. Delalic was specifically asked to do by the supreme command, and what were the things that Mr. Delalic had on his mind, without being given instructions by the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I don't know with whom he was communicating at that time, but he just said the supreme command, which at that time was called main staff. He told me what this was concerning, and in passing he also told me, "I'm going to write this down and I am going to send it off quickly, and you go up there and help out," because during this time we had combat operations in progress. We were on a plateau which was sheltered -- it was a cover, and the observation post, which we used, was out front where certain number of officers were positioned and they were monitoring the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, hear anything said by the supreme command to Mr. Delalic? If "yes," please tell me what you heard. If "no," please just state that. Did you yourself hear anything the supreme command said to Mr. Delalic on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: This part of paragraph 1, he mentioned that succinctly. He said; "they're asking of me to transmit to the municipal staff of the Konjic defence to take written statements from these prisoners at Celebici." But as he had said; "I am also going to include the things that concern our combat activities, so that I would not have to draft a separate document." And that was the extent to which we were able to communicate at that moment. After that, I went to see how the officers at the observation post were doing concerning the artillery attacks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, do I understand that you, yourself, did not hear anything that the supreme command said and your information comes from what Mr. Delalic told you, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I did not hear anything directly because he had said of the radio transmitter and we did not have additional speakers or something so that I could listen in. There were some other issues which they talked to him about which concerned the conduct of combat operations and I recall that it was that they talked about certain larger losses which we had in the Krupac area and he was -- okay, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, in this order, there's a discussion that the investigative military body should provide a copy of their report to this command. Was such a report ever submitted to the command or you just don't know?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Excuse me, which command?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, let me just ask you another way. Do you know what if anything was done, either by the municipal TO or by Mr. Delalic after this order of the 24th of August?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Delalic took no steps in that regard as far as I know. And our command received no report concerning this activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, you already stated that you, at the time, were unaware of the 28th of August document from Mr. Delalic to the commander of the Celebici prison, so I won't ask you about that. But, there's a reference to a particular written order from the supreme command headquarters and I am asking you, with respect to Celebici prison, did you ever see any written order from the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I really did not see one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, you would agree with me that lifting the siege of Sarajevo was, in 1992, the most important military task for the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And because of that, the supreme command obviously wanted to ensure that the Tactical Groups had the means to be effective?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: It did everything they could.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And that included when it was seen that there was a need for it, authorisation for the Tactical Group commanders to issue orders to municipal headquarters about intelligence matters? Is that correct? I think you've already testified to this effect, I am just making sure that I am correct.

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I saw that document and I stated that it followed all the events relating, all the events that took place and they relate to the intelligence information and the information that followed which spelled out and asked of everyone to step up their activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I don't want to cut you off, but I think you explained this in direct. So now I am asking you just a very specific question. It is correct that because of the need, which you've already explained, the supreme command authorised the Tactical Group commanders to issue orders to municipal headquarters about intelligence matters? That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I consider this order too as a transmission of an order that is a notice on the part of the supreme command, even though the intelligence work is very unique and extremely important for the preparations for the following attempts at lifting of the siege that is for the further tasks of tactical groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Let me just clarify then. It's your opinion that because of the prior directives from the supreme command about intelligence orders, any further orders by the tactical group commanders about intelligence matters, all of such orders, were, in effect, transmission orders, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: May I ask you to ask me a very specific question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir. You indicated in your direct that after a particular incident where Mr. Catic was hurt, there was a directive from the municipal headquarters to cooperate with tactical group commanders about intelligence matters, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: This was a standing task of the municipal defence staffs because Tactical Group 1, as well as all the other groups, of course, was an exclusively combat unit and --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I just, if I understand you correctly, there was, in effect, a standing obligation on municipal headquarters to cooperate with Tactical Groups about intelligence matters. And under this standing obligation, Tactical Group commanders had authority to issue orders to municipal headquarters about intelligence matters? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Direct orders in a sense of command and control, they did not have. But, they had a possibility to notify, to request. However, taken into account that before this order, which was transmitted, a directive was issued, a directive on intelligence activity in the area of the front lines so that this order too, as well as the previous orders which we have been explaining here, are transmission orders from the superior command to the municipal defence staffs.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir, let me move on. Now you're aware that as part of the continuing efforts to lift the siege of Sarajevo, when the JUG operation commenced, the JUG commander was given authority by the supreme command to determine for itself what units from various municipalities would be used? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, you would agree with me that the supreme command could give a tactical group commander additional tasks?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Regarding intelligence support.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, you would agree with me that the supreme command had authority to give a tactical group commander any task that the supreme command wished to give? Would you disagree with that?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: Yes, he could.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: And are you aware, for instance, of a well-known occasion in the fall of 1992 when the supreme command tasked Mr. Delalic with the matter involving the arrest of Juka Prazina, Bosnia military commander? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: You never heard anything about Juka Prazina being arrested in the fall of 1992?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I heard it in conversation that he was arrested. But by whom or why, that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Do you know where Mr. Prazina was imprisoned after he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I do not know, and I would request that you do not ask me any questions about the Prasina case because I do not know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir. Now, sir, I assume at the time -- well, I assume that given your position as deputy commander in the urgent combat activities that were going on, it was not unusual for Mr. Delalic to have communication with the supreme command without you knowing exactly the nature of the communication? Did you know the nature of every communication between Mr. Delalic and the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I believe that I knew everything that concerned the activity of the Tactical Group 1. But a commander always reserves the right to communicate to his subordinates the things that he chooses to communicate.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Thank you, Your Honours, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel, I only have two questions for you. First, you said at it one point a HOS unit was subordinated to the Tactical Group 1 at one point and you also indicated where it was located. Can you just clarify, for what period of time was this unit subordinated to Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: I do not know the exact number of days, but it was a short engagement of this unit during the Operation JUG.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With respect to the question, "which units from the wider area of your activity were subordinated to a tactical group?" I only want to ask you whether in the course of the Operation JUG, the units from Konjic and Jablanica were subordinated to your tactical group?

utterances.speaker: Pilica Sucro
utterances.text: They were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Colonel. We're very grateful for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: And this is the end of your testimony, you are discharged. Can we have your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: May we have the next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: (No translation).

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat? The microphone was not on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just ask for clarification from the registrar. Prosecution Exhibit 230, has that been admitted? It's the appointment order of the typist that the witness recognised. And I believe it's already been admitted, but if not, I would request that it be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It has not been tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I would tender Prosecution Exhibit 230. I'm sorry that I didn't do it before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Through who are you tendering it? The witness is not here. It doesn't really matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The commander making the point that it was his own typist for a temporary period. How is it really relevant? How does it shed any light on the command responsibility of Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Or that he can appoint very good staff or he may not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If you read the appointment to assist in the administrative tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, among other things, Your Honours, it would be relevant because it refers to the basis for Mr. Delalic's authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He had the authority to appoint his own typist. Admittedly he was a commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Would you please invite the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I call Mr. Ekrem Milic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please swear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may take your seat, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir, will you please just pull up your chair a little bit so we can hear you better. Thank you. Sir, will you please introduce yourself by stating to the Court your full name?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I am Ekrem Milic, son of Emin Milic and my mother is Hajrija Isanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. Milic, will you tell me where and when you were born?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I was born on 8 January 1959 in the Rogatica municipality in Eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is your ethnic group and your citizenship, sir?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I am a Bosniak and a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, I want to personally thank you even though you were not scheduled for this week, that you were able to adjust your schedule so that you could appear before this Tribunal. Mr. Milic, what is your profession?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: For 17 years I have been a journalist.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was your education and where did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I received all my education in Sarajevo, primary school, the high school and I studied at the school for political science at university and I majored in sociology. And I also have courses in philosophy at the school of philosophy of literature and several Croatian languages as it was called at that time. Or several Croatian or Croat-Serb languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. Milic, can you tell me where you worked until April 6th, 1992? And what was your profession at the time?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Let me first answer the second part of the question. I was a journalist. Officially my official position was a correspondent for a news organisation from Belgrade called Borba, which had about six or seven different editions, both daily newspapers and magazines. I also worked for several media outlets in Bosnia-Herzegovina on a freelance basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milic, I believe that elucidates your professional involvement officially. Mr. Milic, can you now tell me something that is of interest for us here, where were you between April 1992 and April 1993? If you can just sketch it out for us so that we can lay the foundation for the next few questions that I am going to ask of you.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I was in Innsbruck, Austria, at the time of the aggression against my country. And believing that all this was going to end very quickly, I returned to Belgrade with a plan to then go, continue on to Sarajevo. And then when I realised that this was not to be, I turned around and went back to Austria and from there to Croatia to a town called Funtana. It's a small town near Porec in the Istria Region.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, I indicated a longer period of time for you. When you went to Croatia, did you spend all this time in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was in the latter part of April of '92 and I stayed in Croatia as a refugee all the way up to June of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You just answered my next question. You were a refugee. Mr. Milic, during your stay in Croatia, were you able to pursue your profession, either on a regular or occasional basis, that is, to work as a journalist?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: As you know, a journalist never stays still. I actively pursued it on my own for my own sake. I did a lot of research and I followed events, but I did not have any professional involvement in Croatia and that is I could not even try to get one. I believe that it's very clear what the situation was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milic I am just waiting for the interpretation, not because I am not clear about what you were saying. Can you now tell me whether in the period while you were in Croatia, which was April, 1992, and as you just specified up until about June of 1993, did you ever during that period go to Konjic or to Sarajevo through Konjic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: That was my desire, but, unfortunately, I did not. It was not viable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will rise now and resume at 4.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mrs. Residovic, you may proceed with your witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I remind you, sir, that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, to my last question before the break you answered that in 1992 you did not visit Konjic, Sarajevo or Bosnia-Herzegovina, but I would ask you, did you still, as a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina, follow what was going on in that country?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes, to a large extent.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us in which way you were doing that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I was listening to the radio all the time, changing stations repeatedly, meaning that during the evening I was able to get the signal of the BiH Radio. I also followed a programme of the Croatian radio and television, and during the evenings I tried to get the signal of Radio Belgrade, which was at times possible in Croatia, and also the press.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that would be enough. Since you have told us where you were as a refugee, did you during that period go to Zagreb and did you meet with people from Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, starting with May, 1992, because in Zagreb we had the best organised detention centre -- I'm sorry, collection centre for the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a journalist and a human being, you can tell us about that period in 1992, and you could assess on what the standpoint of the Croatian media was towards the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. So can you tell us how you saw all those informations in the Croatian media?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Professionally speaking, I think this was a period of truthful reporting by the Croatian media, that is, April and May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, at any moment, feel the change in reporting of the Croatian media towards the things in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What type of evidence do you want this witness to give? Go straight into what you want him to say, because I don't think any of this is relevant to what you are doing here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What propaganda was going on against your client and what steps he took to counter, instead of going into all of that. It's not necessary for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, I believe we were warned by the Chamber, in full right, because we should skip over things that the Chamber already better knows. On this change of tone of the Croatian media, do you have any knowledge that there was a certain propaganda directed against Mr. Delalic. But prior to your answer, first of all, did you know Mr. Delalic in 1992?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: No, I did not know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Delalic's name in Croatian media, and at what time and, also, if you did, what was the context?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I registered the appearance of that name for the first time during the combat operation which was aimed at lifting of siege of Sarajevo. I think it was called JUG 1992. Until then, I wasn't even paying that much attention. There were mainly reports on successes of our troops around Konjic and so on, Mostar, Duvavo, Livno, front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were following information, was this news of Mr. Delalic done in the negative or a positive way?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I would say neither. It was impartial. Normal I would call it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise to you and to the Chamber, because I can see you are following the interpretation, so you stop in the middle of a thought. I forgot at the beginning to warn you to monitor or to follow the interpretation in the headphones, because we have simultaneous interpreters interpreting what we are saying. So, please, can you speak, speak slowly, and you need not pay attention to the sound and wait for it to interrupt you. But, please, wait with your answer until the interpretation of my question is over. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. And I will try to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise again for not mentioning this before. Mr. Milic, did you, in May, 1992, watch a Croatian programme under the title "Slikom na Sliku"?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: This programme had a very large audience in Croatia. It was on regularly, on a weekly basis. I did not see all of it. Some of them I saw later on through certain video recordings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, at the time when the programme was shown in May, 1992, did you see the particular one which had Mr. Delalic as a guest?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, not in its direct transmission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, did you ever in Croatia meet any of the brothers of Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. That was at the beginning of 1993, and within a period of three or four months I met three of his brothers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the reason for you meeting the first brother, and can you tell us the name of this brother you met in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: First contact with one of his brothers was through Mr. Vejsil Mujkanovic. That was at the beginning of 1993. And we met after I expressed my desire to take a more active role in the work of the Bosnian crisis centre in Zagreb, trying to give my own contribution to preventing or stopping, giving an end to a campaign which was stepping up in the area of Konjic, where the members of the TO and the BiH Army issued significant successes on front line. But, in Croatia the propaganda already took on a negative tone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I had been warned that the name of the person mentioned was not put in the transcript was Vejsil, but since we are going to mention this brother again, we need to clarify it right now. If I understood you correctly, in that crisis centre for Bosniaks you wished to work as a journalist to counter influence to the propaganda. Did you then learn that his brother Vejsil was looking for somebody in that capacity to try to stop -- give an end to that campaign against Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes, after I had a talk with the secretary, Mujkanovic Mohamed was his name, and through our conversations and feel we had about the things going on, as well as my desire to bring the true situation of Konjic into light of day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said you knew the late Vejsil. Without going into further detail, Mr. Mikamic Mohamed, did he enable you to get in contact with Zejnil Delalic's brother?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes, and we did that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you learn from Vejsil on that first meeting? What did he inform you about, and what did he wish you to do?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: See he had authentic information and correct ones. He wanted a denial concerning the campaign that was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Vejsil tell you that he maybe himself tried to do something in connection with the campaign?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: There were no specific conversation about that, but he wished at any cost for the truth to be brought out. Of course, then I suggested that we should gather people who have quality and reliable informations to organise a press conference, and collect video recordings, if possible, unify that, present it to both Bosnia-Herzegovina, population in Croatia, to the Croatian journalists, as well as to foreign journalists accredited in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I know, Mr. Milic, that you are not a psychiatrist, but a journalist, but when you spoke with Vejsil, did you notice a worry or anxiety in him, or was that a normal conversation which required your usual social manners?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: He was very anxious. He was afraid for his relatives in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and his own life in Zagreb, because that was literally the time of lynchings. There was a campaign against the Delalic family.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, during that conversation with Mr. Vejsil Delalic, did he say anything to you about Zejnil Delalic's reaction to this campaign, because in its entirety it referred to him?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: He also had his crisis, moments of crisis, according to Vejsil's statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you wanted to collect data about the events, because you were not a direct participant. Did Vejsil, in connection to that, tell you that you should meet with somebody from Vienna, or did he maybe direct you to somebody else who could give you such information?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: After my suggestion, after I asked for the procedure of collecting as much data as possible, tapes, videotapes, Vejsil promised that he would see to it, and that he would find me associates or co-speakers who could tell me the real truth about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, did he fulfil the promise given to you? Did you meet with somebody?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes, relatively quickly. A brief period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber who did you meet with and where?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I met a man with the last name of Ciso, came from Vienna, or maybe that was his nickname. We were together for several hours. We spoke. I told them my opinion, what needed to be done, and insisted on the speed of going forward, but I also had a precondition that I receive all the information in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, did you receive information you requested, and who brought it to you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: It was brought by Ciso and Dzemal Delalic, another brother to Zejnil, who was supposed to have come earlier in mid January, but he did not have the Croatian passport. And then at the end of January I received about 20 to 30 videotapes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, since the issue here was of propaganda and the newspapers, did you collect articles published about Mr. Delalic at that time?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I would usually receive them from Vejsil, because he was collecting it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you could put it briefly. What was -- what were the articles saying of Zejnil? Before I give my interpretation of the text, I hope you will not interpret all of them, and I am just asking you to briefly tell us what it was about. I believe you understood me, so would you please tell me what you found necessary to say to the Chamber before your answer to my question.

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: My opinion was that it was an orchestrated campaign which was thoroughly planned, directed against Zejnil Delalic and Konjic in general.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you said this introductory part, what did the press release say? Can you cite a few sentences? How did the press make Mr. Delalic look like, if you can remember? How did it portray him?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I would divide that into three categories: Co-operation with the Serbs, and at the same time a KOS associate being proclaimed a Serb spy; activities directed towards creation of an unfavourable climate in order to strain relations between Bosnia and Croatians; and then, finally, the third, and the most serious category, is lie. I would quote their term from the press, referring to the escape of the -- by using the Chetnik helicopter to the Serb territory, which was absolutely untrue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was his treatment of Serb prisoners also mentioned in the media at that time, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a somewhat funny and absurd situation, but presented very skilfully in terms of propaganda. At that time Zejnil Delalic was releasing Serbs from the prison and the camp, even though I know that he was not in a position that he could do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, after Ciso and Dzemal Delalic brought you 20 or 30 cassettes, as you put it, did you review those cassettes and did you do something about it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: At the same day I sort of sped through them, fast forwarding, just so that I could find out what material was there, what was available.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Milic, after this speedy review, as you put it, of the material, did you see whether this material referred to Zejnil Delalic or to something else?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: No, the material in general was about the events in the area between Konjic and the attempt to lift the siege of Sarajevo. For certain operations different material was used. That is, footage from Croatian television, footage from Serb television, footage from the Bosnian television and footage of the local Konjic television. And some footage from private sources, obviously of amateur type.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, did you know who owned the cassettes which were brought to you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is not usual that the witness should ask questions, but what do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Just for clarification purposes in terms of the ownership. Ownership in terms of copyright or in terms of the possession of it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am asking you what you knew in 1992, to whom did the cassettes belong? Who was the proprietor of these cassettes?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: To me, they were the property of Dzemal Delalic, Ciso. I cannot recall his first name. And the authors, that is copyright belonged to all these television outfits which I have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, having reviewed all the material, speedily as you testified before this Tribunal, what did you do with it or did you do anything with it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: My first reaction was that all these needed to be called, shortened and edited into one or two working cassettes, after which I would make or edit the final cassette or tape. And the idea was that this should be a documentary feature of sorts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Given the idea that you just explained to us, did you at some time obtain what you wanted? In other words, did you obtain a reduced tape, reduced video material and who did you get it from?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I obtained it about maybe 15 days after that initial conversation. Ciso and either Dzemal or the late Sefik. I believe that it was Ciso and the late Sefik who brought me these two tapes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Was that the end of your work or did you start working with this material as a journalist?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: That was the time when I started. I reviewed it very carefully, analysed what needed to be highlighted, create a script. It is to create and edit, it is an editing script. That is what excerpts were going to be put together in what order. It took me five to seven days of thorough and intense work. And in the end, I put together my own commentary and the script for this final product which was to be presented at the press conference.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, if I understood you correctly, you now had video material previously from what Vejsil Delalic brought you and you, yourself, were able to get some articles from the Croatian press. But my question is, when you met with Vejsil, Sefik and Dzemal Delalic, did you learn other details and do you know whether some of them were also participants in the events in Konjic in 1992?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Ciso went there several times. Dzemal stayed there for a longer periods of time. And Sefik, the late Sefik as a volunteer, spent several months in different areas of Bosnia, but travelling around. I think it was because he was involved in logistics. In fact, I know that he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So you had different sources of information for these events, media, videotapes and testimonies some of the participants of the events in Konjic. Did you then say to Ciso and Sefik what your intention was? You told us that you were supposed to do the editing script and so on, but were you supposed to report to Zejnil's brothers on what you were supposed to do with it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I asked him and I was disappointed by what I got. Zejnil was completely unaware of what we were engaged in.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, even though you realise that Zejnil was not aware of what you were engaged in, did you compile a script which was to counter the propaganda or some other material that you intended to present at this press conference?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes, I compiled a script and I also gave suggestions as to the way in which those two raw videotapes certain excerpts be shortened further and be arranged so that they are in accord with my script. And I suggested it should not last more than, or run more than 60 to 80 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this cassette put together in Zagreb and were you present when it was edited based on the suggestions that you've given by Zejnil's brothers and other persons involved?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: No, the cassette was not put together in Zagreb. These cassettes were edited and produced in Vienna.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, you just said that you produced this editing script. That you gave suggestions, such as that the running time not exceed 60 to 80 minutes if I understood you correctly. Did you eventually receive a copy of the cassette based on the instructions which were suggested?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, did you view this cassette and were you satisfied with the work that was done?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did review the cassette personally. I expected that it would be done better and in a more professional way. There were many imperfections there, both in terms of just bad editing to blatantly bad audio. That is, speaker's voice.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, regardless of the fact that it was poorly edited and poorly read, was the material which you had suggested to be included in a cassette actually present there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes. From the first to the last word, everything was taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me how did you entitle this tape which was put together according to your concept and with the text which you provided for the visual excerpts?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: There were several working versions, which is understandable. Finally, it ended up with this title, "War in Bosnia-Herzegovina. "

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact that this videotape was put together in an unprofessional way, but what did you suggest for the ending of the videotape given that you provided suggestions for all parts of it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: I definitely wanted a recording and I wanted Mr. Zejnil Delalic to appear on camera. That is the person who, thanks to the Croatian propaganda machine, allegedly fled in a Chetnik helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your tape was supposed to be denial of sorts. Did you include the fact that he arrived in Vienna the day after he left Konjic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was. But following that there was another excerpt. Another excerpt which I have never talked about with either Dzemal, Ciso or anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now what excerpt are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: It was Zejnil's message to the public of Bosnia-Herzegovina, to his friends, to his collaborators, that he was there, that is in Vienna. That he had nothing to do with Serbs. And as far as I knew, this video was -- and it was Dzemal who gave me this information, Dzemal Delalic, was supposed to, through certain channels, be brought to Sarajevo and presented to our own public there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I did not understand you very well. You mean the message that Zejnil was sending to the public was supposed to be taken to Sarajevo or the entire videotape?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: It was just the message, Zejnil's message.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, do you know or did you give any suggestions before you resumed work on this videotape to inform Mr. Zejnil Delalic of your effort? And do you know where he was at the time?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: While we worked at a fast pace on it, both the preparations and the putting together of the videotape. It didn't even cross my mind to inquire about Mr. Delalic's whereabouts, even though I knew that he was in Vienna.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the videotape was put together, did you suggest that it be shown to Mr. Delalic and was it done?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: It was only later that I asked Dzemal whether Zejnil had seen this tape. He told me that he had not seen it yet and that they wanted to surprise him with it once the entire material was put together.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, let's try to pace ourselves up to take the cue from you. Once you received the final edit of the cut of the videotape, do you know whether someone, Dzemal or someone else, showed this videotape to Zejnil Delalic? And do you know what his reaction to it was?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: According to me, it was, for us, it was a defeat. He completely rejected my intention and my idea. But as a consolation of sorts, he thanked me for effort. He opted to get redress in a legal way and this is what he pursued. Apparently he hired an attorney.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, I would now like to turn to your script, to the text and comments that you compiled. And did you present the activities of Zejnil Delalic during 1992 in a truthful manner?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: This is a very difficult question. There has been a lot of exaggeration there. A lot of attempts to respond to this counter campaign with equal means. Certain facts from the field do not correspond to my comments on videotape.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, you're a journalist. Every professional has a certain ethics. When in a propaganda piece, which is so biased, when untruthful facts are presented, do you respond in kind trying to counter that propaganda?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: In a war all means are allowed. And by that very fact, it applies also to the journalistic profession.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, in compiling your comments, did you base them on real or true events which you exaggerated in a way as you put it? Or you did not have such a foundation in real events?

utterances.speaker: EKREM MILIC
utterances.text: The real foundation and my inspiration for this approach to the work on this videotape were, on the one hand, an orchestrated and well-conducted campaign on the Croatian media, which was very effective. And, on the other hand -- I was waiting for the information of the people who were in the field with whom I was in contact steadily and a very important source, which was voice of America radio programmes. Which reported in a very balanced way on the events in the region.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. That would be enough about the foundation. Your Honours, would this be a convenient time to stop for today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's 5.30. We'll adjourn until Monday to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 8th day of June, 1998.
